Bug_Title: "wait(...)" should be used instead of "Thread.sleep(...)" when a lock is held
Bug_Details:
In a multithreaded environment, a thread may need to wait for a particular condition to become true. One way of pausing execution in Java is Thread.sleep(…​) .
If a thread that holds a lock calls Thread.sleep(…​) , no other thread can acquire said lock. This can lead to performance and
scalability issues, in the worst case leading to deadlocks.
Bug_Explanation: The code uses Thread.sleep(1000) while holding a lock on an object. This prevents other threads from acquiring the lock, which could lead to performance issues or deadlock. The correct approach would be to use lock.wait() in a loop that checks for the condition, which would release the lock while waiting.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test invokes the showBug method, which starts two threads that hold a lock and call Thread.sleep(1000). This misuse of Thread.sleep while holding a lock can lead to performance issues or a deadlock, triggering the bug as intended.
Test_Run_Result: Runninng test will fail system because of infinite loop.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test fails with an infinite loop, indicating that the use of Thread.sleep while holding a lock prevents condition changes from being detected by other threads, confirming the bug described.
